final_answer:
PROPERTY TAX DISCREPANCY REPORT - SAGUARO HOLDINGS / WHITMORE CAPITAL PORTFOLIO (Ironwood A, Desert Ridge B, Arcadia C)
To: Buyer (Whitmore Capital Partners LLC) deal team. Compared: Seller's Disclosure Statement dated 3/5/2024 (unsigned copy) ("SDS"); Maricopa County Treasurer records generated 4/15/2024 for each APN ("County"); Broker portfolio workbook ("Broker"). Purchase price $14,850,000. The PSA, title commitment and leases were not supplied.

1. BOTTOM LINE
(a) Seller's 2023 tax figures for all three parcels are wrong. Each matches the prior-year (2022) bill, not the 2023 bill. Total 2023 burden per County is $182,237.41 vs $167,642 disclosed/underwritten: understated by $14,595.41 (8.7%).
(b) Three undisclosed items are material: (i) Property B carries an active Community Facilities District (CFD) assessment lien, $3,812/yr, which the SDS denies; (ii) Property C's second-half 2023 taxes are shown delinquent ($19,743.22 as of 4/15/2024) and (iii) Property C had a 2020 tax lien sold at tax-lien sale and redeemed in 2022, which the SDS omits while representing clean status. Property B's first-half 2023 installment was also paid late (penalty).
(c) Property C's building area is 16,750 SF per Assessor vs 18,200 SF in the SDS and Broker (1,450 SF, 8.0%). Zoning for A and B differs between SDS and County.
(d) Broker NOI and cap rates rest on the understated taxes and should be restated (Section 6).
Caution: items marked VERIFY rest on a County printout that states it is informational only and is not a tax clearance or lien search; confirm with official certificates and the title commitment.

2. DISCREPANCY MATRIX (SDS = Broker unless noted)
Property A (301-42-087A)
- 2023 total tax: SDS/Broker "approx. $79,500"; County $84,746.10 (primary $51,049.41 + secondary $33,696.69). Understated $5,246.10 (6.6%). $79,500 approximates TY2022 ($79,318.44). Broker's own components ($51,049 + $33,697 = $84,746) contradict its $79,500 total, indicating the total was carried over, not computed.
- FCV $5,890,000: matches. LPV $4,712,000: matches.
- Payment: SDS "current, timely": consistent (all installments paid before due; 2nd half paid 2/26/2024).
- Zoning: SDS MU-2 (Tempe); County C-2 Commercial General. Conflict. VERIFY with City of Tempe zoning verification letter (County is not the zoning authority, but the label conflict must be resolved before relying on "permitted use/no nonconformity").
- Rent roll (Broker): suite areas sum to 39,900 SF, exceeding 38,400 SF GBA by 1,500 SF; stated occupied SF 33,408 is inconsistent with listed occupied suites (34,908). Occupancy (87%) and SF figures need an as-built measurement.
- Acquisition year: SDS 2017; Broker 2016 (A and B years appear swapped between documents).
- Lease type: SDS Sec. 9 describes NNN/CAM generally; Broker rent roll shows Suites 100-220 as Modified Gross, so tax increases are not fully passed through at A.

Property B (215-19-344B)
- 2023 ad valorem tax: SDS/Broker $51,720; County $54,965.58. $51,720 is the TY2022 ad valorem figure ($51,720.38). Understated $3,245.58.
- Special assessment: SDS "none; to Seller's knowledge not in any CFD" and Broker "None/$0"; County shows Desert Ridge CFD No. 2008-01 assessment of $3,812/yr, active, levied since TY2009, a continuing lien that "runs with the land" (County cites A.R.S. 48-721 - VERIFY citation). It was paid with each second-half installment through 2023, so Seller had actual knowledge. Total burden $58,777.58 vs $51,720: understated $7,057.58 (13.6%). The SDS Sec. 4.2 "no ... other encumbrances" and Sec. 11 table ("Special Assessments: None") are also contradicted; the assessment also should appear as a title exception.
- FCV: SDS/Broker $3,400,000; County TY2023 $3,640,000 (TY2022 $3,420,000). Understated $240,000 (6.6%). Matches neither year. Broker LPV $2,720,000 vs County $2,912,000. Broker's primary/secondary amounts ($30,592/$21,128) reverse-engineer to $51,720 using the understated values.
- SDS also says secondary tax derives from the limited value; County says secondary tax is levied on FCV (primary on LPV). Minor but shows the SDS value basis was not taken from the bill.
- Payment: SDS "no delinquencies... consistent record of timely payments"; County: first half due 10/1/2023, paid 10/14/2023 with $274.83 penalty ("PAID - LATE"); prior years on time. Note: the County's own table says delinquency begins after 11/1/2023, so the penalty-after-due-date treatment is internally inconsistent; it should be explained by the Treasurer. Either way "timely" is inaccurate.
- Zoning: SDS I-1 Industrial Park; County C-2 (Intermediate Commercial). Conflict. A flex/warehouse use with roll-up doors and a dock may not be permitted in a commercial district. Obtain City of Scottsdale zoning verification.
- Acquisition year: SDS 2016; Broker 2017 (see A).

Property C (170-28-061)
- 2023 total tax: SDS/Broker $36,422; County $38,713.73 (primary $23,708.15 + secondary $15,005.58). $36,422 equals TY2022 ($36,422.50). Understated $2,291.73 (6.3%). Broker components ($23,708 + $15,006 = $38,714) contradict its $36,422 total. FCV $2,785,000 and LPV $2,228,000: match.
- Payment status: SDS "all taxes current... good standing"; Broker "All Taxes Paid". County (4/15/2024): first half paid 9/25/2023; second half $19,356.86 DELINQUENT, interest $386.36, total due $19,743.22, accruing $8.48/day. At the SDS date (3/5/2024) the second half had only just come due (3/1/2024); the SDS may have been literally accurate on that day, but the Broker "all paid" claim and the SDS "supplement promptly" undertaking (SDS Sec. 10) mean Buyer should demand payment or a closing credit. Reliability issues in the County record: (i) it states delinquency after May 1, 2024 yet "delinquent since March 2, 2024"; (ii) 45 days x $8.48 = $381.60, not $386.36. I could not access A.R.S. 42-18052/-18053 to confirm statutory delinquency dates and interest mechanics (see Unresolved); get a Treasurer payoff letter. Unpaid current-year taxes are a lien senior to the deed of trust and Buyer's title.
- Tax lien history: SDS Sec. 3.3/4.3 "no tax liens" and "good standing"; Broker "None". County: TY2020 second-half ($8,214.30) delinquent; lien certificate CP-2022-0017834 sold at the Feb. 2022 sale to Copper Basin Investments LLC, recorded 3/15/2022 (Inst. 2022-0214508); redeemed by Seller 6/3/2022 ($8,761.92); released 6/18/2022 (Inst. 2022-0487312). The lien is released, so "no tax liens" is literally true today, but the omission of a delinquency and tax-lien sale during Seller's ownership contradicts the SDS's clean-history framing for C (and the SDS's blanket certification of completeness). Pattern: a prior delinquency plus a current delinquency at C. Also note TY2020 total ($16,428.60) is about half of TY2021 ($34,118.60): ask Seller why. Also "Copper Basin" appears as a lien purchaser and as tenant name Copper Basin Insurance Group at A (related-party check recommended).
- Gross building area: SDS/Broker 18,200 SF; Assessor 16,750 SF (verified in 2017 re-inspection and Oct. 2022 review). Difference 1,450 SF (8.0%). Price per SF rises from $181.32 to $197.01 at the Assessor figure. Either the Assessor has under-measured (tax benefit to Seller; potential re-measurement and back-assessment/tax increase risk) or Seller overstates area (valuation and rent roll impact). Order an ALTA/ASCM survey and BOMA measurement.
- Vacancy: SDS says Bay 6 (westernmost, about 2,400 SF) is vacant; Assessor says Bay 4 (about 2,200 SF) is vacant; Broker rent roll says Bay 4 vacant at 3,100 SF and Bay 6 is leased (Canyon State Tax, from 4/1/2023). SDS 83% occupancy is arithmetically consistent only with about 3,100 SF vacant (2,400 SF vacant would be 86.8%). Broker summary shows leased 15,106 / vacant 3,094 vs rent roll 15,100/3,100. Which bay is vacant, and its size, must be confirmed by estoppels and a site walk.
- Parking: SDS about 58 spaces; Assessor about 62.
- Special assessments: none; consistent.

3. PORTFOLIO-LEVEL BROKER ERRORS
- Broker summary occupancy 90.5% vs 89.7% computed from its own rent roll (70,614/78,700 = 89.7%); the portfolio leased SF in the Tax/Summary tabs (70,614) differs from the rent roll subtotal (70,608) because of Property A's and C's SF errors.
- Broker "Annual Gross Revenue (Est.)" exceeds in-place base rent: A $624,000 vs $590,652; B $386,750 vs $386,200; C $268,800 vs $221,650 (C overstated by $47,150, 21%). Portfolio revenue estimate $1,279,550 vs rent roll $1,198,502.
- Broker "Total ad valorem" figures at A and C do not equal the sum of its own primary and secondary lines.

4. RESTATED UNDERWRITING (Broker revenue and 30% opex assumptions held constant; taxes replaced with County 2023 totals)
A: NOI $352,054 (Broker $357,300); cap 4.89% (4.96%).
B: NOI $231,284 (Broker $238,342); cap 5.32% (5.48%) using $58,777.58; $235,096 / 5.40% if only ad valorem is counted.
C: NOI $149,446 (Broker $151,738); cap 4.53% (4.60%).
Portfolio: NOI about $732,785 vs $747,380; cap 4.93% vs 5.03%. At Broker's 5.03% cap, $14,595 of annual NOI is about $290,000 of value, before any C revenue correction. If C's revenue is limited to the rent roll ($221,650) and 30% opex, C NOI falls materially further (about $103,000 after $38,714 tax; cap about 3.1%). These are illustrative; NNN reimbursements may recover part of the tax at B and C but not at A's Modified Gross suites, so leases must be reviewed.

5. LEGAL FRAMEWORK AND SIGNIFICANCE (preliminary; PSA not reviewed)
- The SDS invokes A.R.S. 33-422. To my understanding that statute concerns an affidavit of disclosure for certain sales of land in specified counties (parcel-split/unsubdivided-land context) and is not a general commercial-property disclosure mandate; I could not retrieve the text. Buyer's remedies therefore should be anchored in the PSA (Seller representations, survival, indemnity, closing conditions), the SDS certification (Seller states it will be relied upon and that misstatements may create liability), and Arizona common law: fraudulent concealment/misrepresentation requires a known, material fact; negligent misrepresentation (Restatement (Second) of Torts 552) is also available. Seller had actual knowledge of B's CFD (paid annually), B's late payment, and C's 2020 lien (Seller redeemed it); A's and B's 2023 second halves were paid by Seller in February 2024, before the SDS date.
- The SDS contains disclaimers (actual knowledge only; buyer to verify; "detailed disclosures control" over the summary table). These weaken but do not defeat claims where the facts were within Seller's actual knowledge; they also mean Buyer cannot claim reasonable reliance on figures it was told to verify. Treat as due-diligence findings and negotiate now rather than rely on post-closing claims. Check PSA for a non-reliance clause, knowledge definition, cap/basket, survival, and due diligence termination deadline. The SDS (3/5) pre-dates the PSA (3/8) it cites and the buyer acknowledgment and seller signature are blank: confirm the executed version and whether it was incorporated into the PSA.
- Arizona context to verify: current taxes are a lien on the parcel (the County cites A.R.S. 42-17153); a CFD assessment lien survives transfer; there is no reassessment on sale but FCV is reset annually (TY2024 notices of value issued early 2024 are not in the file and could raise B and C values and taxes; the 5% LPV cap limits primary tax growth).

6. RECOMMENDED ACTIONS
1. Written notice to Seller/Broker listing each discrepancy; demand corrected, signed SDS and supplement; demand rationale for 2022-equal figures.
2. Obtain official Treasurer tax certificates and payoff letters for all three APNs; require payoff of C's 2023 second half (and interest) at or before closing with a credit; confirm no certificate of purchase is outstanding.
3. Property B: obtain CFD No. 2008-01 documents (term, remaining balance, any prepayment option); require title exception review; price adjustment for the lien and the $3,812/yr cost (capitalized at 5.0% about $76,000); consider requiring Seller to prepay the balance if permitted.
4. Pull TY2024 Notices of Value; underwrite 2024 taxes; evaluate appeal rights (Assessor appeals generally must be filed within 60 days of the notice, per County record).
5. Zoning verification letters (Tempe, Scottsdale); resolve MU-2/C-2 and I-1/C-2 conflicts; confirm legal conforming status.
6. Independent measurement of C (and A); reconcile bay numbering/size, parking and vacancy; request estoppels and certified rent roll; restate pricing per SF.
7. Have the broker reissue the workbook with corrected taxes, revenue tied to rent roll, and corrected cap rates; renegotiate price (indicative adjustment at least $290,000 for tax effect, plus C revenue and CFD effects) or obtain a specific indemnity/escrow holdback for tax, CFD and delinquency matters.
8. Extend the diligence period if necessary; reserve rights to terminate under the PSA if corrections are not delivered; add specific representations on taxes, assessments, liens and areas, with survival and no cap for known misstatements.
